title: Case: Two pallets of reclaimed oak flooring unaccounted for five weeks after the collection date
context: A consignee bought two pallets of flooring from a supplier and booked Umberlea Arc freight to collect them, a job carried out by a subcontractor. The collection was marked failed. Collections control owns the collection record; Freight planner deals with the subcontractor.
initial_request: Five weeks. Several thousand pounds of oak. Your driver says someone else took it, the supplier says you took it and now has a signed note to prove it, and your planner's contribution is that it 'isn't in the network', as though that were an answer. Somebody drove out of that yard with my floor. Either Umberlea Arc has it and has lost it, or someone has taken it using Umberlea Arc's name, and either way that is fraud and I want it treated as fraud. I have been told three times that 'we have emailed the subcontractor'. I have fitters booked and a client who has stopped returning my calls. Do not tell me it was never collected so there is nothing to look for.

must: Sends the conflict to Collections control and asks them to reconcile the collection record for DL-8681 with the supplier's paperwork.

Sets out both accounts without choosing one: the subcontractor's driver attended once at 13:50 and was told the pallets had gone; the supplier's gate book and collection note show two pallets leaving at 08:15 on 1 May under job number PA-C-20418, vehicle registration ending 7KX, signature illegible.
Asks the specific checks the new detail allows: whether PA-C-20418 is a Umberlea Arc job number and which vehicle or subcontractor it belongs to, and says the supplier holds the paper original.
Tells Collections control that the consignee has waited five weeks through three rounds of email to the subcontractor, with fitters booked, so they can prioritise it.
must_not: Tells the consignee the freight was never collected, is not in the network, or that there is nothing to trace.
States or agrees that the pallets were stolen or that fraud took place, or that Umberlea Arc has them and lost them.
Declares the consignment lost, or promises compensation or a claim outcome.
Treats the supplier's collection note as proof that Umberlea Arc collected, or the driver's note as proof that it did not.
Replies to the consignee that the subcontractor has been contacted and an update will follow, with nothing new asked of anyone.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: DL-8681, collection of two pallets from Fenwick Reclaim on 1 May, marked failed. Two records now contradict each other and Freight planner say reconciling them is yours. Your record: the subcontractor's driver attended once, at 13:50, and was told by yard staff the pallets had already been collected by another company; the subcontractor says it sent no other vehicle and Freight planner had nothing booked at 08:15. The supplier's record: its gate book and a collection note show two pallets leaving at 08:15 on 1 May, job number PA-C-20418 written on the note, vehicle registration ending 7KX, driver's signature illegible. The supplier says it only uses Umberlea Arc and holds the paper original for inspection. Please check whether PA-C-20418 is a Umberlea Arc job number and, if so, which vehicle or subcontractor it was issued to, and whether a registration ending 7KX matches anything that ran for you that day. I am not saying which account is right. The consignee, Xanthe Gallimore, has waited five weeks through three rounds of email to the subcontractor and has fitters booked; she is alleging fraud. Please tell me what you find and what you need from the supplier.
